history.recommendation_text: The Board reiterates its recommendation that the Administration closely monitor the ongoing recruitment process of resident coordinators to ensure that the posts of resident coordinator and the key posts at resident coordinator offices are filled in an expeditious manner.
history.administration_response: The Administration is already closely monitoring the ongoing recruitment processes for resident coordinator posts to ensure that resident coordinators are recruited expeditiously. As at 20 March 2025, 118 resident coordinator positions were encumbered (91 per cent), 1 was vacant and 11 were covered by a resident coordinator ad interim (8 per cent), the lowest share since the reform and well below the average vacancy rate in United Nations system agencies. Among the 11 resident coordinator positions covered by a resident coordinator ad interim, 2 are pending government clearance, 3 are under recruitment and 5 have been filled, with the relevant candidates approved to begin their duties in the coming months. Of the 12 posts that had been vacant as at December 2024, 2 had been vacant for a long time, for reasons that are not within the control of the Administration, but rather of Member States. The Administration respectfully reminds the Board that the Administration cannot be held accountable for factors that are not within its control. Of the remaining 10 positions, recruitment for 8 had already been completed, with 6 candidates awaiting government clearance and 2 candidates about to be deployed. Government clearance is the prerogative of Member States; therefore, the Administration cannot be held accountable for it. As for the other two candidates, one was deployed on 5 January 2025 and the other was deployed later in 2025, given that his clearance was not received until December 2024, after which he had to complete the required notice period with his previous employer. In conclusion, the Administration can be held accountable only for the fact that, in December 2024, 2 resident coordinator positions of 130 were vacant (1.5 per cent of the total). This fully warrants the closing of this recommendation.
history.board_assessment: Given that the number of encumbered resident coordinator positions was only 114 (87.7 per cent) as at 26 May 2025, with 16 positions (12.3 per cent) to be filled, the Board is of the view that the vacancy issue has not been duly resolved and therefore considers the recommendation to be under implementation.

history.sg_progress: As at 1 August 2025, 117 resident coordinator positions – representing 90 per cent of the total – were filled. One position remains vacant, while the remaining 12 are temporarily covered by resident coordinators serving ad interim. This reflects a vacancy rate that is below the average across United Nations system entities. Of the 12 ad interim positions, five are awaiting the arrival of newly appointed coordinators, who will assume their duties upon the conclusion of the incumbents’ assignments, and the remaining seven are either pending government clearance or are at various stages of recruitment. This data underscores the Administration’s active oversight of the recruitment process, ensuring positions are filled in a timely and effective manner. The Administration considers this recommendation to be implemented and requests its closure by the Board.
